newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World sees oilseeds output deficit in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Oil World sees oilseeds output deficit in 1996/97.

text.p: World production of 10 key oilseeds in 1996/97 was forecast at 255.3 million tonnes, against 258.7 million tonnes of consumption, the independent Oil World newsletter said on Tuesday.
This compared with estimated output of 253.7 million in 1995/96 versus 258.9 million tonnes of usage.
The 96/97 oilseeds area was forecast at 186.6 million hectares versus 188.3 million ha in 1995/96. Yields in 96/97 were pegged at 1.37 tonnes per ha versus 1.35 tph previously.
Oil World said oilseeds were competing for grain acreages, which would stay high as producers sought to bring output and consumption back into balance after tightness in 1995 and 1996.
Higher U.S. soybean crop expectations would be offset by low Latin American stocks and a fall in China's soybean crop in the upcoming season by one million tonnes to 12 million.
This would encourage Chinese imports of beans and products.
Crop estimates had also been reduced for rapeseed in Poland and Canada, and for sunseed in the Ukraine and Russia.
Oil World saw a chance of oilseed, meal and price rises from end-October in response to crop shortfalls and stocks cuts. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
